properties.headline: Blowing Dust Advisory issued August 3 at 2:06PM MST until August 3 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Thunderstorms will initially develop over the Mogollon Rim
and other sky islands of Southeast Arizona, then track southwest
into the valleys of Southeast Arizona and become widespread during
the late afternoon, then move across the lower deserts of Southeast
Arizona through the evening. The stronger storms will produce
organized thunderstorm outflow winds between 45-55 mph, resulting
in dense blowing dust with visibility between one-quarter and
one-half mile and possibly a haboob with near-zero visibility. For
the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions with
temperatures 101 to 106. Major to Extreme HeatRisk is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Tucson Metro Area,
Upper Gila River Valley, Upper San Pedro River Valley, and Upper
Santa Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.
Heat related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat
events.
properties.instruction:
Persons with respiratory problems should make preparations to stay
indoors until the storm passes. Be ready for a sudden drop in
visibility to near zero. If you encounter blowing dust or blowing
sand on the roadway or see it approaching, pull off the road as far
as possible and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights all the way
off and keep foot off the brake pedal. Remember, 'Pull Aside, Stay
Alive'.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 1:43PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert for wildfire smoke has been issued by the
following agencies:

Puget Sound Clean Air Agency
Olympic Region Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for King, Kitsap, Pierce,
Snohomish, and Thurston Counties through 5pm Wednesday August 5 due
to expected wildfire smoke from regional fires. Air quality
conditions are expected to worsen throughout the day today as smoke
begins to mix down to the surface. Particulate matter (PM2.5)
concentrations may reach UNHEALTHY FOR SENSITIVE GROUPS. When air
quality is UNHEALTHY FOR SENSITIVE GROUPS, individuals with health
concerns and pre-existing conditions should reduce exposure and take
precautions. This means limiting time outside, avoiding strenuous
activity, and following tips for cleaner indoor air. Visit
pscleanair.gov and orcaa.org/news-notices for current conditions,
updates, and more information.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 3 at 1:51PM PDT until August 5 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures 100 to 110.

* WHERE...Antelope Valley and nearby foothills.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for dangerous heat illness,
especially for sensitive groups like the very young, the very old,
those without air conditioning, and those active outdoors.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Heat hazards may extend through Saturday.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 3 at 12:04PM AKDT until August 7 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas: Central Susitna Valley and Western
Susitna Valley. This includes Petersville, Cache Creek, Talkeetna,
and communities along the Yentna and Skwentna Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Significant rainfall is expected in the Susitna Valley Monday
August 3 through Wednesday August 5. Current estimates is for
48-hr rain totals to range from 3 to 5 inches in the upper
Yentna, Chulitna and Susitna Basins.

Talkeetna: The heavy rainfall and drainage from high terrain
near the Alaska Range could be impactful to erosion-prone
areas and low-lying or poor-drainage areas throughout the
rest of the Susitna Valley. Small rivers such as Montana
Creek are expected to rise as well, but not to the level that
occurred in late July.

Petersville Area: Small creeks in and around Petersville such
as Peters Creek and Cache Creek could experience flooding,
with the highest water levels expected between Tuesday
morning and Wednesday morning.

Yentna: Larger rivers, including the Yentna and Skwentna
rivers, are expected to crest later, between Thursday
afternoon and Friday morning.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke.

Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy.

* WHERE...Ada, Adams, Boise, Canyon, Elmore, Gem, Owyhee, Payette,
Valley, and Washington Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 2 PM MDT FRIDAY.

* IMPACTS...Everyone may begin to experience health effects; members

properties.instruction:

elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Boise Regional Office at (208) 373-0550

* WHERE...Baker, Harney, and Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL NOON PDT TUESDAY.

weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information

OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

levels.

healthcare provider's advice.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 8 feet
in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion through this evening. Life-threatening
rip currents are likely for all people entering the surf zone
through Tuesday. Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of
the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

Quality Advisory...in effect until 4 PM Wednesday for northern
Klamath and Lake Counties...

combined with northerly winds will cause air quality levels to
fluctuate and could be at unhealthy levels.

young children, people with heart or lung disease, older adults and

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 3 at 12:00PM MST until August 7 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
107 to 118. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Western and Southern Imperial County, including the
Imperial Valley and Salton Sea.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 3 at 12:00PM MST until August 7 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
110 to 115. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...The Phoenix metropolitan area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, Call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 11:25AM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Coeur d'Alene

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Boundary, Bonner, Kootenai, Shoshone, and Benewah
Counties...

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy.

* WHERE...Boundary, Bonner, Kootenai, Shoshone, and Benewah Counties...

* WHEN...Next update 11 AM PDT August 5th.

* IMPACTS...Some members of the general public may experience health
effects; members of sensitive groups may experience more serious
health effects.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Coeur d'Alene Regional Office at (208) 769-1422
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued August 3 at 2:43PM EDT until August 4 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
...HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK IN EFFECT FROM LATE TONIGHT THROUGH
TUESDAY EVENING...

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 9 feet in the surf zone Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected Tuesday.

* WHERE...Washington, Dukes MA, Nantucket MA, and Newport RI
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late tonight
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...greatest risk of strong rip currents Tuesday
will be at south facing ocean beaches.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
The following message is transmitted on behalf of the Wyoming
Department of Environmental Quality, Air Quality Division and the
Wyoming Department of Health.

WHAT...Air Quality Alert for Wildfire Smoke.

WHERE...Southeast Wyoming

WHEN...11am Monday to 11am Tuesday

IMPACTS...Heavy smoke from Pacific Northwest Wildfires

HEALTH INFORMATION...The Wyoming Department of Health recommends the
elderly, young children, and individuals with respiratory problems
avoid excessive physical exertion and minimize outdoor activities
during this time. Wildfire smoke is made up of a variety of
pollutants, including particulate matter and ozone, which can cause
respiratory health effect. Although these people are most
susceptible to health impacts, the Department of Health also advises
that everyone should avoid prolonged exposure to poor air quality
conditions.

Quality, Air Quality Division offers near real-time air quality data
for Wyoming's monitoring stations and health effects information to
help the public interpret current conditions. Current air quality
conditions across the state of Wyoming can be found at

Department of Environmental Quality, Air Quality Division, and the
Wyoming Department of Health.

* WHAT...Air Quality Alert for Wildfire Smoke.

* WHERE... Yellowstone National Park, the Bighorn Basin, the Wind
River Basin, the Absaroka Mountains, the Owl Creek and Bridger
Mountains, the Bighorn Mountains, the Rattlesnake Hills and Green
Mountains, Johnson County, and Natrona County.

* WHEN... 11 AM MDT Monday to 11 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Smoke from western United States wildfires continues to
be observed across much of western and central Wyoming. The smoke
is limiting visibilities at times.

HEALTH INFORMATION...The Wyoming Department of Health recommends
that the elderly, young children, and individuals with respiratory
problems avoid excessive physical exertion and minimize outdoor
activities during this time. Wildfire smoke is made up of a variety
of pollutants, including particulate matter and ozone, which can
cause respiratory health effects. Although these people are most
susceptible to health impacts, the Department of Health also advises
that everyone should avoid prolonged exposure to poor air quality
conditions.

CURRENT CONDITIONS...The Wyoming Department of Environmental
Quality, Air Quality Division offers near real-time air quality data
for Wyoming's monitoring stations and health effects information to
help the public interpret current conditions. Current air quality
conditions across the state of Wyoming can be found at
http://www.wyvisnet.com/.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued August 3 at 11:50AM EDT until August 3 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...For Rip Currents, the beaches from Cape Hatteras to
Oregon Inlet. For Longshore Currents, the beaches from Oregon
Inlet to Surf City.

* WHEN...From this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 5:15 PM Monday.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ THIS
EVENING FOR SOUTHWEST NORTH DAKOTA, AND FROM 11 AM MDT /NOON CDT/
THIS MORNING TO 8 PM MDT /9 PM CDT/ THIS EVENING FOR PARTS OF
SOUTHCENTRAL NORTH DAKOTA...

...

.Critical fire weather conditions are expected across southwest and
parts of south central North Dakota today. Northerly winds will
increase to around 25 to 30 mph this afternoon, with gusts as high as
40 mph. Relative humidity could fall as low as 25 percent this
afternoon.

* AFFECTED AREA...Mercer, Oliver, Morton, Grant, and Sioux.

* TIMING...Until 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...North winds around 25 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE SOUTHERN
WILLAMETTE VALLEY MONDAY AFTERNOON AND EVENING DUE TO DRY
CONDITIONS AND NORTHERLY WINDS GUSTING UP TO 25 MPH...

...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE WESTERN
COLUMBIA RIVER GORGE TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH WEDNESDAY EVENING
FOR DRY CONDITIONS AND EASTERLY WINDS UP TO 40 MPH...

The National Weather Service in Portland has issued a Red Flag
Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect
from 11 AM Tuesday to 8 PM PDT Wednesday. The Fire Weather Watch
is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Washington, Fire Weather Zone 636 Western
Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington.

* WINDS...East 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. Winds will be
strongest Tuesday morning through early Tuesday afternoon, and
again Tuesday night through early Wednesday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-20 percent. Relative humidity
values will be lowest Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday afternoon.
Poor overnight humidity recoveries are expected Tuesday night
with maximum relative humidity values ranging between 35-45%.

* IMPACTS...Conditions may be favorable for rapid fire spread
which may threaten life and property. Use extra caution with
potential ignition sources, especially in grassy areas.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of the
above conditions can contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Flathead, Lake, Lincoln, Beaverhead, Sanders, Deer
Lodge, Silver Bow, Granite, Mineral, Sanders, and Missoula counties
in effect until 9AM on 08/04/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Columbia
Falls, Frenchtown, Lewistown, Libby, Missoula and Thompson Falls are
Unhealthy.

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Butte are Unhealthy
for Sensitive Groups.

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Dillon, Great Falls,
Hamilton, Helena, Malta and Sleeping Giant are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 3 at 9:17AM CDT until August 6 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 37.3 feet, Widespread lowland flooding occurs. Minor
roads are closed. Airport Road boat ramp near Live Oak County
Airport is flooded and closed. Major flooding occurs in the River
Creek Acres Subdivision, with several feet of water and several
homes flooded. Residents in the J.I. Hailey Subdivision at Jones
River bend have trouble getting out as water covers much of
Antelope Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Monday the stage was 37.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Tuesday, then fall below flood stage midday Thursday. The
river will then continue to fall to 12.8 feet Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 3 at 5:08AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A storm moving in from the Bering Sea will bring widespread,
prolonged rainfall to Southwest Alaska through Tuesday.

- Rain amounts: Through Tuesday afternoon, widespread rainfall
amounts of an additional 1 to 2 inches are expected across
Southwest Alaska, with locally higher amounts possible (up to 3
inches for the Western Alaska Range).

- Timing of heaviest rain: For Kuskokwim Delta and Bristol Bay,
this morning. For Alaska Peninsula and Southwest interior (Lake
Iliamna region and along the Western Alaska Range), Monday into
Tuesday.

- Winds and water levels: For coastal areas from west of
Dillingham to the Western Capes (including the communities of
Togiak, Goodnews Bay, and Platinum), southerly sustained winds
of 25 to 35 mph will persist through Monday afternoon. This
could bring water levels up to 1 foot above the mean high tide
line. Winds will be strongest early Monday morning.

Preparedness: Check the forecast for the latest updates, especially
if you plan to be outdoors or traveling. Along Bristol Bay, beware
of gusty winds and high water levels along the coast.

NWSheadline: WIDESPREAD PROLONGED RAINFALL THROUGH TUESDAY AND STRONG ONSHORE WINDS THROUGH MONDAY

WHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.

WHERE...Moffat, Rio Blanco, Routt, Jackson, Grand, Larimer and
Boulder Counties. Locations include, but are not limited to Craig,
Meeker, Rangely, Steamboat Springs, Walden, Granby, Hot Sulphur

likelihood of respiratory symptoms in sensitive individuals,
aggravation of heart or lung disease and premature mortality in

heart or lung disease, older adults, and children should reduce
prolonged or heavy exertion.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Walton, Bay, Gulf, and Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Mountains; East Bay Interior Valleys; Santa Clara Valley Including San Jose; Eastern Santa Clara Hills; East Bay Hills
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 2 at 10:52PM PDT until August 3 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures ranging from 95 to 105.

* WHERE...The Santa Clara Valley and The Eastern Santa Clara Hills,
The East Bay Hills and Valleys, and North Bay Interior Mountains.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and in
heat-sensitive industries.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles.Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 2 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, elevated water levels, widespread moderate to heavy rain,
and southerly winds are expected across the area. Water levels
could rise 1 to 3 feet above the mean high tide line in coastal
areas of the Bering and Chukchi Seas. Rain totals from Sunday
afternoon through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from
1 to 2 inches south of the Bering Strait and from 0.5 to 1 inch
north of the Bering Strait. From Sunday afternoon through Tuesday
night, southerly winds will gust to 30 to 40 mph. Those in coastal
areas should take extra precautions to ensure that belongings are
properly secured ahead of these increasing winds and water
levels.

NWSheadline: Elevated Water Levels, Widespread Rain, and Wind to Start the Week

properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, it will bring widespread moderate to heavy rain and
southerly winds across the area. Rain totals from Sunday afternoon
through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from 1 to 2
inches across most of the Western Interior. River levels will rise
with this rainfall, although no flooding is expected. From Sunday
afternoon through Tuesday night, southerly winds could gust as
high as 40 mph in the Lower Yukon and Upper Kuskokwim Valleys,
with gusts over 30 mph possible elsewhere.

an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Monday,
August 3, 2026.

on Monday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a

avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.
